# Introduction

PhiSpace ST applies PhiSpace to spatial transcriptomics (ST). A single-cell
RNA-seq reference with annotated cell types is used to score every spatial
location of the query for every cell type. The scores are continuous, so a
location that contains several cells, such as a 10x Visium spot, can score
highly for several cell types. The scores of all locations can then be
clustered into **niches**: groups of locations with a similar cell type
composition.

In this vignette the reference is single-cell RNA-seq of the mouse
somatosensory cortex and hippocampus (Zeisel et al., 2015), and the query is a
10x Visium section of the mouse brain. The method is described in Mao et al.
(2026), *Cell Reports Methods* 6(8), 101483
(<https://doi.org/10.1016/j.crmeth.2026.101483>).
The introductory vignette, `vignette("PhiSpace", package = "PhiSpace")`,
explains the PhiSpace scores in more detail. Larger case studies, including
imaging-based and sequencing-based ST platforms, are on the
[PhiSpace website](https://mao-lab-org.github.io/PhiSpace/).

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("PhiSpace")
```

```{r packages, message = FALSE}
library(PhiSpace)
library(SpatialExperiment)
library(scRNAseq)
library(STexampleData)
```

# Data

## Query: a Visium section of the mouse brain

`r Biocpkg("STexampleData")` provides a 10x Visium section of the mouse brain
as a `SpatialExperiment` object. We keep the spots that cover tissue, use gene
symbols as row names, and log-normalise the counts.

```{r query, message = FALSE}
query <- Visium_mouseCoronal()
query <- query[, query$in_tissue == 1]
rownames(query) <- rowData(query)$gene_name
query <- query[!duplicated(rownames(query)), ]
query <- logNormTransf(query)
query
```

## Reference: single-cell RNA-seq of the mouse cortex and hippocampus

The Zeisel dataset in `r Biocpkg("scRNAseq")` contains 3,005 cells with seven
major cell types in the column `level1class`.

```{r reference, message = FALSE}
reference <- fetchDataset("zeisel-brain-2015", "2023-12-14")
reference <- logNormTransf(reference)
table(reference$level1class)
```

The reference and the query are both RNA-seq counts, and both are
log-normalised in the same way. We keep the genes measured in both.

```{r genes}
genes <- intersect(rownames(reference), rownames(query))
length(genes)
reference <- reference[genes, ]
query <- query[genes, ]
```

# Annotation

`PhiSpace()` fits a partial least squares (PLS) model of the cell types on the
reference and scores every spot of the query. The number of components,
`ncomp`, is set to the number of cell types. With `nfeat = 300`, PhiSpace
selects the 300 most important genes for each cell type and uses the union of
these genes in the final model.

```{r phispace}
query <- PhiSpace(
    reference, query,
    phenotypes = "level1class", refAssay = "logcounts",
    ncomp = 7, nfeat = 300
)
reducedDim(query, "PhiSpace") <- normPhiScores(reducedDim(query, "PhiSpace"))
head(reducedDim(query, "PhiSpace"), 3)
```

`normPhiScores()` centres the scores of each cell type at their median and
scales them to a maximum absolute value of 1, so that the scores of different
cell types are comparable.

# Cell type maps

`VizSpatial()` colours the spots by the score of one cell type. With
`censor = TRUE`, scores below their median are set to the median, so that
the colour scale shows only the spots where a cell type is enriched.

```{r maps, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 8}
cellTypes <- c("pyramidal SS", "pyramidal CA1", "oligodendrocytes",
               "interneurons")
maps <- lapply(cellTypes, function(ct) {
    VizSpatial(query, reducedDim = ct, censor = TRUE, ptSize = 1,
               legend.position = "none") +
        ggplot2::scale_y_reverse() +
        ggplot2::coord_fixed() +
        ggplot2::ggtitle(ct)
})
ggpubr::ggarrange(plotlist = maps, ncol = 2, nrow = 2)
```

The pixel row coordinate increases downwards in the image, so we reverse the
y axis to show the section in its usual orientation.

Pyramidal SS scores are highest in the cortex, along the top and right edges
of the section, and pyramidal CA1 scores in a thin arc inside it, in the
hippocampus.
Oligodendrocyte scores are highest beneath the cortex and in deeper regions,
consistent with white-matter tracts. The reference contains only cells of the
cortex and hippocampus. Spots in other brain regions therefore score highest
for the most similar reference cell types; here, many deep spots score highly
for interneurons.

# Niches

`findNiches()` clusters the spots by their PhiSpace scores with k-means, after
a principal component analysis of the scores. Its `seed` argument makes the
result reproducible without changing the random-number state of the session.

```{r niches}
query <- findNiches(query, n_niches = 6, verbose = FALSE)
table(query$spatial_niches)
```

```{r nicheMap, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 5}
VizSpatial(query, colBy = "spatial_niches", ptSize = 1.5,
           legend.title = "Niche") +
    ggplot2::scale_y_reverse() +
    ggplot2::coord_fixed()
```

The heatmap shows the scores of all spots, grouped by niche, and so the cell
type composition that defines each niche.

```{r nicheHeatmap, fig.height = 6}
plotPhiSpaceHeatMap(
    reducedDim(query, "PhiSpace"),
    queryLabs = query$spatial_niches,
    cluster_columns = TRUE,
    name = "Score"
)
```

Most niches score highly for one or two cell types. For example, one niche
scores highly for pyramidal SS and covers the cortex, and another scores
highly for oligodendrocytes. The niche map and the cell type maps above show
the same regions.
